chunks: From him, from ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
Al-Aḍḥā is two days after the Day of Sacrifice in Minā, and one day only in the towns.

The correct way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them to mean that the days of sacrifice during which fasting is not permitted are three days in Minā, and one day in the rest of the lands; because after the sacrifice day, fasting is permitted in the other towns, whereas that is not permitted in Minā except after three days. And that which indicates this is:

key_terms.أَيَّامَ النَّحْرِ: the days associated with sacrifice in which fasting is restricted
key_terms.الصَّوْمُ: fasting, whose permissibility is the legal issue under discussion
key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: the festival period of sacrifice being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.بِالْأَمْصَارِ: in the towns or regional settlements outside Minā
key_terms.بِمِنًى: in Minā, where the ruling differs from other places
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ: the three-day period in Minā during which fasting is not allowed
key_terms.يَوْمِ النَّحْرِ: the Day of Sacrifice, the central reference point for the legal count

ai.seo_question: How many days after Yawm al-Naḥr is fasting prohibited in Minā versus other towns?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling of the days following Yawm al-Naḥr, distinguishing between Minā and other locations. It explains that fasting is prohibited for three days in Minā, while in other towns the prohibition applies only to one day, reconciling the reports on this issue.
